races.name: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: River Jordan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Phillip Makin ridden by Connor Beasley who has winning form on good going at this trip; placed twice from two starts at Thirsk's five furlongs, this is his most natural environment, and he is the runner most likely to occupy the genuine back-of-the-field position the map projects.

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: One run only — seventh on good going at this trip — so the form book offers almost nothing to work with; Fahey's yard has fired in 1 winner from 45 runners over the past fortnight, and the unknown quantity here is whether that single effort underrepresented ability or was representative.

runners_data.name: Suenicora Star
runners_data.note: Finished last on her only start over six furlongs on standard Tapeta for Brian Ellison, a trainer who has had a quiet 14-day spell; stepping to turf on good ground and dropping to five furlongs raises questions about whether this is an improvement scenario or an experimental outing.

runners_data.name: Bacha
runners_data.note: Fahey runner with a fifth on standard Tapeta last time out — its truest inclination is to race held-up at the back, though the surplus of hold-up horses in this field means it is unlikely to find that position naturally, placing it in a compromised tactical spot throughout.

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts on good ground at five and six furlongs give Battle Fever the most relevant proximity form in the race; Kevin Stott is a canny jockey for Ryan and with a style that can be flexible, Battle Fever could slot in second or third on the heels of Palm Reader to make a forward move from a genuine tactical position.

runners_data.name: Red Blue Point
runners_data.note: Debutant for James Tate and Silvestre De Sousa — going, trip and style are all unknown quantities; Tate runs first-timers with intent and De Sousa is one of the shrewder judges of pace, but without a single data point this horse cannot be assessed with confidence.

runners_data.name: Palm Reader
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over five furlongs at Thirsk last time out — same course, trip and going — for an in-form trainer who has fired in 1 from 7 in the past 14 days; he wears a tongue-tie and his natural front-running style maps perfectly to this race shape, making him the pivot around which every other runner's chance is constructed.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.note: Has finished fifth and eighth in two starts on good ground at this trip for Kevin & Lauren Frost, whose yard is in lively form with 3 winners from 13 runners recently; its true running style is held-up, but the volume of hold-up types in this field means Articulate is likely to be forced to race closer to the pace than suits, tempering its chance in any shape that rewards genuine late closers.

races.paceDynamic: Palm Reader is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the gates, should be allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control every fraction on good ground at Thirsk's straight five furlongs. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — River Jordan, Bacha, and Articulate all want to come from off the pace — meaning the pace Palm Reader sets is unlikely to be pressured early, creating a genuinely sustainable gallop rather than a test of stamina. Battle Fever and the unknown quantities in Red Blue Point and Unbeatable Fame may track up prominently but neither has the profile to force the issue and disrupt Palm Reader's rhythm. The race shape strongly favours a horse who can race prominently or lead, because a single front-runner on good going over five flat furlongs at Thirsk — where the draw and pace dynamics historically reward those who travel into the race — is a significant tactical advantage; the hold-up brigade face a stern task if the fractions are controlled and the gallop never truly collapses. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Bacha and Articulate are genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, and River Jordan is most likely to secure the genuine back-of-the-field berth, while Bacha and Articulate will race closer than their natural inclination allows.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Palm Reader Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Palm Reader breaks cleanly and sets an uncontested, metronomic gallop that no rival is willing or able to challenge.
scenarios.body: Palm Reader's uncomplicated front-running role on flat, five-furlong Thirsk — in his natural style, carrying the tongue-tie, for an in-form trainer — means he sets every fraction and never has to find an extra gear off a bend or cover ground; the hold-up horses behind have no short straight to pounce through traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking runner sits two lengths off Palm Reader's hip and produces a superior finishing effort in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Battle Fever has shown placed form at this trip on good ground and is bred to quicken late from a stalking position; if Palm Reader's fractions are slightly brisk, a close-tracking rival picking up early in the final furlong will have the race to themselves as the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Palm Reader's pace is genuinely hot and the front end weakens in the final 100 yards, allowing hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: River Jordan has form in similar conditions and is handled by an in-form jockey in Connor Beasley, so if the pace unexpectedly collapses late, a strong finisher from the rear can pick up; however, because Bacha and Articulate are true hold-up types forced closer than ideal, the genuine late run will most likely come from River Jordan alone.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is erratic, runners bunch in the straight, and the race degenerates into a sprint for the line with no clear tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: In a condensed finish on flat ground, unexposed or lightly raced horses like Red Blue Point or Unbeatable Fame — where form lines are thin — could outrun their odds in a messy scramble; this scenario is the least likely given the clear pace advantage Palm Reader holds but cannot be entirely discounted with several unknowns in the field.

watchPoints.text: Palm Reader — if he breaks cleanly and is allowed to bowl along uncontested, every other runner is immediately at a tactical disadvantage on this flat, straight five furlongs; watch whether anything challenges for the early lead from the gates.

Bacha and Articulate — both are natural hold-up horses who will be squeezed out of their preferred position by the weight of similar types in this field; if either is found racing awkwardly in the early stages trying to find space, their chance deteriorates sharply.

Red Blue Point — a Tate/De Sousa debutant on a card where going is uniformly Good; first-time runners from this yard can be well-prepared but the complete absence of form data means any early waywardness or greenness could compromise its race entirely.

Battle Fever — the most relevant placed form on comparable ground and trip of any horse in the chasing pack; watch whether Kevin Stott elects to sit directly behind Palm Reader or allows a gap to develop, as his positioning in the first furlong will signal how much he trusts the draw and the gallop.

races.name: William Hill Summer Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Roger Varian and Silvestre De Sousa; recent form is patchy and his OR=102 makes him the highest-rated runner, but a 44-day break and just one win in similar going temper confidence — the style advantage of leading uncontested is significant here.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Prominent type stepping down sharply from 10-11f trips where she has scored; Lexie Clarkson claims 7lb for a yard showing zero wins from three runners in the past fortnight, and the trip looks on the short side for this mare — the OR drop to 97 is the main appeal.
runners_data.comment: Two unplaced efforts in his last four starts make Dain Ma Nut In hard to fancy, and our rating ranks him eighth of eleven; he does have experience over today's trip and conditions, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight years who continues to run well on good ground, winning last time over 7f at this course for Michael Dods and Connor Beasley — the combination have strong Thirsk form and tracking the leader is exactly what suits him over this extra furlong.
runners_data.comment: Northern Express brings a timely 22-day break and course-winning fitness into this, scoring last time out and holding a strong rating edge over his rivals; has run over today's trip and going, and 137 lb is the one test of his claims.

runners_data.name: Pure Legend
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old has a lone career win on soft/heavy ground and the switch to good at Thirsk on a 69-day absence raises a flag — prominent style suits the race shape but the going record (1 place from 11 runs on good-ish) is a real concern for his chance.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner last time out, Pure Legend arrives here after a 69-day break with questions to answer about fitness, though that victory shows he retains ability; unexposed enough to leave that form behind if sharpened by the break.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's seven-year-old holds a busy recent record but the form string 890000 speaks for itself — hold-up style will need the pace to lift sharply and his OR has drifted badly; Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim offers minimal compensation.
runners_data.comment: Witch Hunter has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 102 — nine pounds above his official mark — suggests he's significantly better than his recent winless sequence implies; the risk is that six starts without threatening the frame makes it hard to trust him fully.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Faye McManoman partners this four-year-old who has been racing at 10-12f and even a Polytrack spin recently; dropping back to 8f on good ground for Nigel Tinkler, headgear not indicated, and she will need to settle and produce a late run from the rear — not ideally placed in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tuscan Hills at least brings experience of today's trip and conditions, and a fifth last time out hints at modest improvement; carrying 133 lb from stall 10, he remains one to watch rather than trust at this level.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old is at his best racing prominently and has two recent wins at this distance on good going, but the field is too crowded up front for him to claim his natural berth — his STYLE_FIT tag and fade tendency in finishes mean he is best watched rather than relied upon here; Tudhope's quality is the main positive.
runners_data.comment: Mirsky showed his best when winning five starts back, and he returns here fit on 28 days' rest, carrying 133 lb from stall 5 with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; the risk is that his last two outings have both been well below that level.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's five-year-old has a solid record at 8f on good ground with a recent second here, and prominent style suits this race shape perfectly — Cam Hardie is a capable jockey for this track and distance, making him one of the more straightforward options in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Swivell nevertheless caught the eye with a second last time out and a rating of 99 suggests he merits serious respect from stall 2; the risk is that fourth and unplaced efforts before that hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Dosman
runners_data.note: Oli Rix's gelding is a genuine prominent racer whose best form over 8f on standard and good ground is clear from his history; placed in a race where five prominent types are chasing two positions, he will almost certainly settle further back than ideal — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and Jonny Peate will need to make swift decisions at the start.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claim) rides this Ed Dunlop seven-year-old who holds genuine course-and-distance form, including a win at Thirsk on good ground — hold-up style needs the pace to open up but he is one of the more credible beneficiaries if the front-runners tire.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out gives Sterling Knight some recent credibility, but two unplaced runs between that and his win four starts back make him inconsistent; he has run over today's trip and going, and 131 lb is a stiff ask if he's to land a blow from stall six.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's four-year-old arrives on the back of two consecutive wins at this trip on good ground at Goodwood, and his hold-up profile means he depends on a strong enough gallop to close into; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride and the upward trajectory in OR terms is the standout angle in the hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Priapos won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, but an unplaced effort last time out is hard to ignore, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Jeddaal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has won at 7f and 8f on good-to-soft and good, carrying just 9st 2lb — he is a true prominent type whose redistribution to midfield is a genuine tactical disadvantage; if George Downing can get him into a prominent position at the break he becomes interesting, but the STYLE_FIT tag and field crowding make that uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Jeddaal has winning form in recent starts — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back — but ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, he faces a stiff ask at 122 lb from stall seven after 49 days off, with only experience over today's trip and going to encourage.

races.paceDynamic: Fondo Blanco is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger willing or able to press him hard from the off, he should settle into a comfortable, controlled gallop down the Thirsk straight mile on good ground. The pace will be honest but not scorching — Fondo Blanco's Roger Varian stable has him in good hands with Silvestre De Sousa, and the combination is unlikely to either crawl or sprint, setting up a steadily run race that will test finishing quality rather than raw stamina. Behind the leader, the prominent positions are genuinely overcrowded: Mirsky, Dosman, and Jeddaal are all natural front-to-prominent types who have been mapped to midfield precisely because the berths ahead are already taken, meaning several horses will race slightly further back than suits them. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner dictating a fair but manageable tempo on good turf — strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-up running style who can track the pace without being caught wide, as late closers from the rear will need the gallop to sharpen up significantly in the final two furlongs to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fondo Blanco Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Fondo Blanco bowls along unchallenged and the pace remains honest enough that close-tracking prominent types can maintain contact throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: Fondo Blanco controls the tempo from the front and the field strings out behind him, with Northern Express and Mr Swivell the closest threats tracking him through the middle stages; on good ground at Thirsk where front-runners have a solid record over a mile, a horse that leads without being pressed can easily see out the straight. Prominent-style horses who travel smoothly in second and third are ideally placed, with hold-up horses needing an unlikely late surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Fondo Blanco sets just enough pace that Northern Express or Mr Swivell, tracking closely throughout, reel him in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The front-runner establishes a rhythm that looks comfortable but has used just enough energy to be vulnerable in the last 100 yards, allowing a horse that has shadowed him throughout to produce a decisive late stride. Northern Express has strong course-and-distance form on good going and Connor Beasley is an accomplished front-rank jockey, making him well positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Fondo Blanco goes too hard early under pressure from others attempting to get position, dramatically lifting the tempo and leaving the front rank vulnerable.
scenarios.body: A fast-run first half stretches the field and burns out the prominently-placed horses, allowing Sterling Knight or Priapos to emerge from the rear group with a sustained run down the straight; Priapos has been in sharp form with two recent wins on good ground and travels well for Oisin McSweeney. Sterling Knight also fits this profile with his hold-up style and positive course record, though he needs the pace to genuinely collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent berths cause significant early jostling and Mirsky, Dosman, or Jeddaal manage to break smartly enough to reclaim their natural position.
scenarios.body: The scramble for position in the early stages produces an uneven tempo that unsettles the fancied front-runners and opens a gap for one of the redistributed prominent types to slot in and run a race that suits them better than their mapped position suggests; Jeddaal is lightly raced at three years old and has real ability on good ground, making him the most dangerous of this trio if he gets a clear run. However, the STYLE_FIT discounts mean this scenario carries the least weight.

watchPoints.text: Fondo Blanco — watch at the start: if he breaks cleanly and Silvestre De Sousa sends him straight to the front uncontested, the entire race is set around him and his ability to conserve energy through the early stages becomes the key factor.

Mirsky, Dosman, Jeddaal — all three are natural prominent types who cannot physically all get the position they want; watch for a scrappy, contested middle section in the first two furlongs as they try to move up, which could artificially lift the pace and benefit the hold-up horses.

Pure Legend — the going is good at Thirsk and his entire place record at similar conditions is one place from eleven runs; if the ground rides fast, he is at risk of running below his OR before the field even turns for home.

Priapos — arrives on a two-timer and is one of only a handful of runners whose recent form is genuinely upwardly mobile; watch whether he gets an unobstructed run on the outside in the straight, as his hold-up style is reliant on a clear passage.

Northern Express — Connor Beasley knows Thirsk well and this horse has strong course form; watch whether he positions immediately behind Fondo Blanco from the off, which would put him in the ideal spot to challenge in the final furlong without expending energy early.

races.name: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Le Samourai
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old showed a win on turf at 7f on Standard ground and is bred for this step up to a mile; racing prominently under Edward Greatrex, the Good going is confirmed fine and this track-surface combination suits a horse that travels well early and kicks.|

runners_data.name: Morty Robinson
runners_data.note: A six-year-old veteran with an OR of 120 in a novice context, but his sole recent run — a distant 13th over 7f at Sandown — offers little confidence, and the fade-in-finish flag raises doubts about his ability to sustain an effort over this mile.|

runners_data.name: Ben Travato
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's three-year-old was beaten sixth at Goodwood over 7f on Good and his natural instinct is to race off the pace, though in this field the surplus of hold-up horses means he is unlikely to secure that position and must race closer than ideal — a meaningful discount applies.|

runners_data.name: Test Run
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's runner has two runs on Good ground at a mile-plus, finishing fourth and fifth, so the trip and going pose no fresh concerns; Billy Garritty partners a horse who wants to come late, but the steady pace being set may not generate enough of a finishing kick opportunity.|

runners_data.name: West Sleekburn Lad
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's three-year-old is the sole front-runner and will command the lead unchallenged, but both recent runs on Good ground produced defeats and the fade-in-finish tag suggests he may be vulnerable when the race quickens; Cam Hardie must judge the fractions carefully to give himself any chance.|

runners_data.name: Brighton Beach
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this three-year-old with Daniel Tudhope aboard — a strong booking — and the horse has placed at 10f on Good ground; fundamentally a hold-up horse, the congestion of similar types in this field forces Brighton Beach into a midfield berth rather than its preferred late position, blunting its natural weapon.|

runners_data.name: Regal Desire
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's consistent filly has run second twice on Good ground at a mile, showing genuine affinity for this trip and surface; racing prominently under Ben Robinson, she is perfectly suited to the tactical shape this race is expected to take and her consistent placed form suggests she will not be far away.|

races.paceDynamic: West Sleekburn Lad is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace pressure from others in this seven-runner field, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good ground at Thirsk over a mile. Regal Desire and Le Samourai will look to track closely in prominent positions, creating a compact early order that is unlikely to be disrupted. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Brighton Beach and Ben Travato are both true hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because Test Run is also waiting, meaning at least one or two of those three must race closer to the pace than they would prefer. A lone, uncontested front-runner setting a fair but not punishing tempo over a flat mile on Good ground strongly favours those racing prominently or tracking just off the lead, as the race is unlikely to develop the sustained late sprint that pure hold-up horses require.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If West Sleekburn Lad dictates a measured gallop and those tracking closely produce the winning move at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: West Sleekburn Lad sets fractions that suit horses travelling just behind him, with Regal Desire and Le Samourai well-placed to pounce entering the straight without burning too much fuel chasing a hot pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up horses find a clear run in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Test Run and Ben Travato, if able to find room, could reel in a tiring front group, though both are racing on the shorter side of their comfort zone and must time their runs to perfection.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If West Sleekburn Lad, unchallenged and allowed to bowl along, finds a second wind and the field fails to pick him up.
scenarios.body: A soft, uncontested lead on good ground can occasionally produce an unlikely front-running winner if rivals leave the move too late, and with the field holding multiple hold-up types displaced from their natural role there may be a lack of early challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or a strong headwind into the straight causes chaos and the whole field bunches in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In this low-probability scenario, Brighton Beach — held up by Tudhope for the Haggas yard who have been in decent form — could benefit from late scrimmaging, though its natural style is compromised by the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Regal Desire, who has twice finished second at this trip on Good ground, gets a clean passage tracking West Sleekburn Lad — if she does, she looks the most naturally suited horse to this race shape.

Monitor West Sleekburn Lad's fractions through the first three furlongs; if Cam Hardie is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged he could steal enough of a break that prominent trackers are drawn into chasing prematurely.

Brighton Beach and Ben Travato are both true hold-up horses effectively forced into midfield — if they cannot secure a clear run two furlongs out the congestion could cause interference and materially affect the outcome.

Test Run's two runs at a mile on Good ground are the right profile, but Billy Garritty will need a different pace scenario than this one appears likely to deliver; watch for any mid-race change in tempo that brings late closers back into play.

Le Samourai's step up from 7f to a mile looks a positive development given his breeding under Ralph Beckett, and Edward Greatrex riding out for weight makes this runner worth monitoring in the early exchanges to see whether he settles smoothly in the prominent group.

races.name: Jordan Foy Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old veteran whose best form on Good ground is limited (6/15 runs, no wins), his natural late-running style is further compromised by redistribution into a contested midfield where he is unlikely to find the clear passage he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and again two starts back — wait, the sixth placing two runs ago is the concern — Mondammej is winless in recent starts yet bounced back to second last time, suggesting he retains ability; experience over today's trip and going and a quick 11-day turnaround keep him competitive from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Rotokura Belle won on Good ground at 5f (1W2P in 8 sim-going runs) and Silvestre De Sousa is a major positive, but her natural hold-up style places her in the group of closers who cannot all find the rear berths they need in this field.|

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with poor recent form (8-0-0-6-4-0) and just 2W3P in 12 Good-ground runs over 5f; his natural closing style is squeezed further back than ideal, and nothing in the record suggests he can reverse this pattern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with recent form figures making grim reading, Muker is hard to fancy from stall 12 carrying 132 lb — though he has run over today's distance and going before, and our rating of 78 offers slim cause for hope.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Tim Easterby (2W6P in 8 sim-going runs) with blinkers applied, last ran just 8 days ago suggesting she is in good nick; well-placed to sit behind True Promise and pounce.|
runners_data.comment: Canaria Queen has won once in her last six starts, with a pair of fifth-place finishes sandwiched between that success and a latest second, making consistency the concern; she has run over today's trip and going, and 8 days between runs suggests freshness, but ranked last on our figures she faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Holds one win on Tapeta but no wins on Good turf in 7 sim-going runs, and his natural hold-up style further limits prospects; Bryan Smart's stable is cold (0/4 over 14 days) adding to the concerns.|
runners_data.comment: Castan has won in his last six starts but sits ninth of 12 on our figures, and back-to-back poor efforts — unplaced and ninth latest — make him hard to fancy at this level; he does return on a handy 22-day break with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 6-year-old carries excellent Good-ground credentials (3W6P in 11 runs) and is in strong form (913121); his naturally prominent style suits the expected race shape perfectly and Billy Garritty provides a reliable pilot.|
runners_data.comment: Rock Of England arrives in good nick — a winner last time out and again three starts back — but he is ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, and a 136 lb burden makes him hard to fancy at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 5-year-old shows no sim-going turf form of note and his true closing style leaves him among those unable to secure a natural position at the rear; the 26-day break and a messy recent record (5U5305) do not help.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Accrual does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third three starts back shows he can threaten the frame; the fifth-place effort last time was a solid enough midfield run, though a hefty 135 lb to carry from stall 2 is a clear concern.

runners_data.name: Comic Strip
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's 3-year-old is 33 days since last seen and has only 2 runs on Good ground with no wins or places from them; tongue-plate fitted but the profile looks light for this competitive sprint.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Comic Strip nonetheless showed he retains some ability with a third and a second in recent outings, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 135 lb from stall one, he's a midfield sort whose consistency is patchy but not without hope.

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Fionn McSharry, but her sim-going record is modest (0W1P in 3 runs) and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she carries the burden of setting the pace alone at OR 81 while potentially outrunning her own effectiveness late.|
runners_data.comment: True Promise steps up with solid claims — a winner two starts back and placed a further two starts before that in recent form, he has experience of today's trip and conditions and returns after a 22-day break in good order; the fifth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners George Scott's 6-year-old who has 1W4P on Good ground and sits at the top of the handicap on OR 81; a genuine hold-up horse but better placed than most redistributed types to pick up midfield scraps if the pace truly collapses.|
runners_data.comment: Moulin Booj shaped with promise when second two starts back and third three starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going. Winless in recent starts, but rated highest in the field and carrying 141 lb from stall 11, he returns after 29 days looking the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old is exceptionally consistent on Good ground (2W6P in 13 sim-going runs) and Daniel Tudhope is an excellent booking; tongue visor fitted and the sharp Thirsk 5f is well-known to him, making him the most dangerous of the midfield hold-up brigade.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tiva nonetheless posted a second four starts back and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her firmly in the mix at 139 lb from stall four — the main concern is recapturing that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley also saddles this 5-year-old, who shows 1W3P in 11 Good-ground runs; his true late-running style is the issue — displaced into midfield and unable to get a clear run, his two recent seconds on Good turf came when conditions aligned more cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six, American Bay nonetheless shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back, and has experience of today's trip and going — our rating of 84 marks him as a serious threat here. The main concern is that unplaced effort last time out.

races.paceDynamic: True Promise is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her from the gates on a flat 5f Thirsk track, she is likely to control tempo from the front at a sustainable gallop. Rock Of England and Canaria Queen are the most naturally prominent horses in the field and will look to sit just behind True Promise, creating a compact early order rather than a truly contested pace. The redistribution note is critical here: American Bay, Rotokura Belle, Accrual and Mondammej are genuine hold-up types who cannot all find their natural rear position in a 12-runner sprint, meaning several will be shuffled into an uncomfortable midfield, compromising their ability to produce the late surge their style demands. With a single uncontested pace-setter and Good ground at Thirsk, this race shape strongly favours prominent horses who can travel just off True Promise's shoulder and pounce in the final furlong — pure hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If True Promise dictates an uncontested, even gallop and kicks clear inside the final furlong before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: True Promise sets a sustainable tempo with no one willing to go with her, and the hold-up contingent — many of whom cannot even reach their natural position — find the race over before they wind up; prominent horses just off the pace are the chief beneficiaries if True Promise ties.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If True Promise sets just enough pace to bring prominent-tracking horses to the front entering the final furlong without themselves tying.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England's excellent Good-ground form (3W6P in 11 runs) and Canaria Queen's front-rank consistency make them the most dangerous profiles under this shape; both can track True Promise and sprint past her if she overcooks the front end.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Flyer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If True Promise goes too fast early and the race opens up for a horse tracking at halfway to swoop.
scenarios.body: Tiva and Moulin Booj hold genuine sim-going form at this trip and are the best-qualified of those forced into midfield, able to capitalise if the pace proves stronger than expected; Moulin Booj's class at OR 81 gives him an edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses late and redistributed true closers manage to find an unusually clean passage from the rear.
scenarios.body: This is structurally the least likely outcome: Rotokura Belle, Accrual, Mondammej and American Bay are all competing for the same late-running lane and cannot all get it, and a steady Thirsk gallop rarely gifts closers enough of a gap; only a significant pace collapse makes this viable.

watchPoints.text: True Promise sets the entire race shape — if she is slow away or pressed unexpectedly by Rock Of England or Canaria Queen, the tempo projection changes radically and midfield types gain ground.|
Rock Of England and American Bay are both trained by Paul Midgley; watch for stable intention, as one prominently placed and one in midfield could represent a deliberate two-pronged attack.|

The redistribution cluster of Rotokura Belle, Accrual, Mondammej and American Bay will all be seeking similar late ground — a traffic-management incident in the final 2f is a real risk with 12 runners on 5f.|

Tiva's tongue visor is a notable headgear addition for David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope — if it sharpens her early stride she may secure a better midfield pitch than her natural style would normally suggest.|
Comic Strip's 33-day absence and Castan's 22-day break are worth monitoring in the market; neither trainer is firing at a strong rate over 14 days and fitness questions hang over both.|

races.name: William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Edward Bethell who handles good ground well, though nine placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs without a win at this level flags a tendency to find one too good; Kevin Stott's booking is positive but the OR of 92 means he carries top weight relative to his rivals.
runners_data.comment: Returned a promising second last time out, and Yorkshire has run over today's trip and going before — the weight and draw from stall 16 are the factors to watch, but he shapes as a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa retains the ride on this seven-year-old who has three wins and five places from nine runs on similar going, and his last-time-out second at this course and distance makes him one of the most course-relevant threats in the field; goes well fresh (22 days) and his natural prominent style suits a controlled pace perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Croupier landed a win and was runner-up next time in his recent runs, and has experience of today's trip and going; carrying 134 lb from stall nine, his rating of 100 marks him as the one to beat, though his latest two runs give slight pause.

runners_data.name: Asuka
runners_data.note: The sole designated front-runner, trained in form by George Boughey (three winners in 23 days), and his two wins from three starts on good ground show he handles the conditions; with no realistic challenger for the lead he can dictate terms and control the tempo, which is his single greatest tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Asuka arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and again three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a quick 10-day turnaround suggesting he's thriving; the 134 lb burden from stall two is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's four-year-old won twice on good ground at this trip and was placed twice on soft, but a 57-day layoff and a lacklustre run last time out (16th of 16) temper enthusiasm; if the break has freshened him he has the class to be competitive tracking the pace.
runners_data.comment: Aurora Majesty showed a win and placed efforts earlier in this sequence but has gone unplaced in his last two, and 57 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and stall one is his draw.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's gelding carries a hood and has run consistently without winning across his last six starts on good ground, with no win or place from five runs in similar conditions a significant negative; Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim reduces the burden but the form line reads as one-paced.
runners_data.comment: Angel Hunter has run over this combination of distance and going, and at 22 days he arrives fresh and ready; the concern is that he's been out of the frame in his last five starts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Yankee Dude
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's four-year-old returns after 117 days off and has two wins from five runs at this trip, though both victories came on standard/artificial going at Wolverhampton and his single placing on good was a second at Sandown; the big break is a noted risk but fresh horses with strong SP figures occasionally land here.
runners_data.comment: Yankee Dude hasn't run for 117 days and, ranked 12 of 16 on our figures, is hard to fancy; he does carry experience over today's trip and going, showed a second last time out, and has two wins in his last four starts, but the layoff is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance last time out under a confident front-rank display, and the headgear note (p, presumably a hood) suggests he needs to be organised close to the pace; Richard and Peter Fahey have just one winner in 45 runners over 14 days which is a mild trainer concern, but the recent course-winning form is hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has been unplaced since, and a trainer strike-rate of just 1/45 in the last 14 days is a real concern; he has experience over today's trip and going, though, and returns after 22 days off carrying 131 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's lightly-raced four-year-old holds a genuine win over this trip on good ground, but having been pushed back to a mapped midfield position because of the congestion of prominent types ahead of him, he will need to overcome an unfamiliar race scenario to land this; his natural game is to race in the first three, and anything that prevents that will cost him.

Brighton Boy landed a win four starts back and shaped with promise when second three starts back, but unplaced on his return 35 days ago tempers enthusiasm; he has distance and going experience, yet 130 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: New Image
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's veteran holds a fine record at the trip with two wins and four places from 15 runs on similar going, and Daniel Tudhope is an experienced hand for a horse who prefers to come from off the pace; that said, a genuine hold-up run requires a truly run race, which this pace map does not guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, New Image does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, but his recent form — unplaced last time out and largely out of the frame — makes it hard to get enthusiastic, despite a rating of 88 suggesting some latent ability.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: A natural front-rank racer with strong recent form (1-3-2-2 in last four) but mapped to midfield given the overcrowded prominent zone; Mark Walford's eight-year-old thrives when he can sit handy and the redistribution away from that position is the most significant tactical risk against him here.
runners_data.comment: Ran well when winning last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he carries 129 lb from stall 8 and ranks 11th of 16 on our ratings — form has been patchy in recent starts beyond that latest success.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old wears a tongue-strap and a hood, and has placed in each of his last four runs including a second over this course and trip on good ground; Cian Horgan's 5lb claim helps but this hold-up type needs the pace to be honest enough to bring him into it in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six but back-to-back seconds two and three starts back show he's competitive, and he has run over today's trip and going before; 128 lb from stall 14 and a recent unplaced run are the checks against him here.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's six-year-old has a fading-in-finish flag attached, which is a meaningful negative in a race where the pace may not be truly testing; won once on good ground at this trip but the flag, combined with three blanks from four in recent form, makes him a risk at any price.
runners_data.comment: Obelix won three starts back but has finished fifth in each of his last two, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, the 127 lb burden from stall 15 makes further improvement a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Michael Dods has six winners from 25 in the past 14 days, showing the yard in form, and Glenfinnan won over 1m on good ground last time; Connor Beasley knows the horse and his hold-up style is genuinely that — he can deliver late if the pace provides a target to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Glenfinnan is hard to fancy despite a second last time out brightening his recent form; the ninth three starts back reflects a more typical profile, and he faces a stiff task at these weights even with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: King's School
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's five-year-old carries headgear (tp), placed twice recently at this trip and distance, but only two runs from 15 on similar good ground is a thin sample; Billy Garritty takes the ride and the horse's closing style needs a genuinely run race that this pace map may not deliver at its expected tempo.
runners_data.comment: King's School has shown he can win in recent starts — a winner three starts back, and a second two starts back — but a fifth last time out and a ranking of 16th on our figures make him hard to fancy at the weights here.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old wears a visor, is only seven days off a run, and has five places from 12 outings on similar going; a natural prominent racer who has been displaced to a mapped midfield position by the weight of pace in this field, and his best chance hinges on recovering enough of that ground in the early stages to race closer than his map position suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Woodstock has run over today's trip and going and bounced back to consecutive runner-up finishes in his last two, which offers some encouragement — but ranked 14th of 16 on our figures from stall 10, he faces a stiff task off 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 72) and a genuine hold-up type pushed to a midfield map position because of the volume of closers in this renewal; Gemma Tutty's second representative has no wins from 15 starts on similar going and the combination of redistribution, low rating and a blank recent-form line (0 last time) makes her difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 15 of 16 on our figures, Enola Grey has little in her recent form to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Asuka is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead mandate under Jack Callan, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good ground at Thirsk over seven furlongs. The prominent brigade — Yorkshire, Croupier, Aurora Majesty, Angel Hunter, Yankee Dude and Our Havana — will track closely behind, creating a well-organised early order rather than a pressured scramble, since Asuka is unlikely to be seriously tested for the lead. The field does contain more genuine prominent/prominent-leaning types than the map can accommodate: Brighton Boy, It Just Takes Time and Woodstock are all natural front-rank horses who will be forced wider or deeper than they prefer, with Brighton Boy and It Just Takes Time the most likely of the three to still salvage a prominent berth given their recent form and jockey familiarity. With one honest pace-setter dictating from the front and the gallop unlikely to be truly punishing, this race shape tilts decisively towards those sitting close to the pace in the first three or four lengths — prominent runners travelling smoothly into the straight will have the clearest passage and the best strip of ground, making the P-style profile the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asuka Controls, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Asuka leads at a measured gallop and the prominent quartet tracks smoothly to challenge entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Asuka sets an honest but unforced pace, allowing Croupier, Yorkshire and Aurora Majesty to travel comfortably in his slipstream before unleashing their finishing efforts from the two-furlong pole; the even tempo suits horses with tactical speed rather than a pure late burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Asuka Outstays Challengers
scenarios.trigger: If Asuka's lead is never seriously threatened and the pace-setters behind fail to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Asuka dictates every yard at a comfortable tempo, conserving enough energy to repel late challenges as the prominent horses around him lack the gears to reel in a front-runner who has had it entirely his own way; good ground at Thirsk historically favours a front-runner who controls the fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves quicker than expected and the field strings out, opening a gap for closers to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Andesite and Glenfinnan, both with strong records on good ground at this trip, close relentlessly from the rear as the prominent horses tire; New Image and King's School, genuine hold-up types, also arrive late but need the pace to have been genuinely demanding.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If multiple displaced prominent types — Brighton Boy, It Just Takes Time, Woodstock — jostle for position early and create an uneven, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: The disrupted rhythm unbalances the race and opens the door for a horse who can adapt mid-race, with Woodstock's course-and-distance know-how and Yankee Dude's fresh-horse freshness (117 days off) potentially decisive; unpredictable renewals like this occasionally throw up a wide-draw winner who avoids the carnage.

watchPoints.text: Asuka (front-runner) jumping cleanly and establishing an uncontested lead immediately — if he gets a soft lead the race shape locks in around him and the prominent horses behind are the primary threats.

Brighton Boy, It Just Takes Time and Woodstock all pressing for the same prominent berth in the opening furlong — any scrimmaging among these three displaced horses could unsettle the early order and compromise all of their runs.
Our Havana has shown winning form over this course and trip most recently; if he travels smoothly in the first rank he is the most dangerous immediate challenger to Asuka turning into the straight.
Glenfinnan's trainer Michael Dods is in a notably productive 14-day spell (6/25) — monitor market movement as a potential each-way indicator if the hold-up scenario gains traction.

Obelix's fading-in-finish flag combined with a potentially undemanding pace makes him one to oppose in betting markets, particularly in any scenario that requires a genuine staying effort in the final furlong.

races.name: Vision Pvc Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Charlie Johnston with a solid sim-going record (1W3P on Good), but five of his last six runs have resulted in finishes of 4th or worse; De Sousa takes over in the saddle and at 8 days' freshness this 6yo could be primed, though his 142lb burden is the heaviest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ludo's Landing showed his class with a win six starts back and was third three starts back, and he has distance and going experience to call on; fit from a run just eight days ago and our top-rated runner, he is the one to beat off 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Northern Brave
runners_data.note: Michael Dods 3yo returning after 43 days off — the layoff warrants monitoring — and his best form has come over shorter trips (8f) or on softer ground; stepping up to 1m4f on Good looks a significant ask, and his sim-going record of 0W0P over 5 runs offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Northern Brave landed a win four starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a lively threat from a mark of 75; the main concern is that he has failed to build on that victory in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: La Peregrina
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo has shown real promise with two consecutive runner-up finishes at 12-14f on Good ground, and her sim-going record of 0W2P gives her placed credentials; she is a genuine hold-up horse whose true style sees her racing further back than her mapped midfield position suggests, and that positional compromise could cost her in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat but a genuine danger nonetheless — La Peregrina has finished second in each of his last two starts and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating nudging him ahead of his official mark; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 3yo has headgear noted (p) and was last seen 14 days ago, a confident freshness cycle; however his last five runs have all resulted in finishes between 4th and 9th on Good ground, and like La Peregrina his natural instinct to race from the rear means he may not secure his preferred berth in this all hold-up field — tempering expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in defeat to remain a genuine threat, That Darn Cantor returns on a quick turnaround of 14 days, has run over today's trip and going, and 128 lb is workable — though winless in his last five starts, that persistent mid-division pattern is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up style, this 1m4f Thirsk contest has no confirmed front-runner, meaning the field will likely crawl into the first bend before someone is forced to take it up under pressure from connections. The pace is expected to be modest early, creating a bunched, tactical affair that develops into a sprint finish off a slow tempo — a scenario that typically suits whoever has the highest cruising speed rather than the truest stayer. La Peregrina and That Darn Cantor are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, as the rear of the field is more congested than it appears; in reality, one of these two is most likely to end up with the lead by default rather than design. This race shape — a crawl turning into a dash — most favours the horse with the sharpest change of gear over this extended trip, lending the decisive advantage to whichever runner can produce the strongest sustained late run from a handy position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawl Then Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is pedestrian throughout and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: With no genuine front-runner, the field idles along before a sudden burst in the straight rewards whoever delivers the sharpest acceleration; this is the most probable shape given all four runners' natural tendencies. La Peregrina's recent placed efforts over 12-14f on Good ground and strong sim-going record give her the profile to pounce from a handy mapped position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one runner reluctantly takes up the running from the outset and dictates a true pace
scenarios.body: That Darn Cantor or La Peregrina, pushed forward by circumstance, could find themselves alone in front setting a measured gallop that suits a strong traveller who can kick off the bend. Ludo's Landing, with six-year-old experience and Silvestre De Sousa in the plate, is best equipped to track and pounce if a solo leader gets detached and ties.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than anticipated and the field strings out, leaving a closing run viable
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race over 1m4f on Good ground would play into the hands of a true hold-up horse who can finish powerfully; Ludo's Landing's sim-going record of 1W3P over 15f on Good is relevant here. Northern Brave, at just 3 years old with a win at Hereford on Heavier ground, is less proven in this scenario but could outrun his OR=75 mark if conditions suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes interference and positional battles throughout, turning the race into a rough-and-tumble affair
scenarios.body: With four horses all wanting to sit off the pace, jostling for position could lead to a messy race where momentum is disrupted and the most streetwise or experienced horse prevails. Ludo's Landing's age and experience at 6 years, combined with De Sousa's tactical intelligence, gives him the edge if the race becomes physically and tactically demanding.

watchPoints.text: Watch for La Peregrina and That Darn Cantor to be squeezed for position at the start — with four hold-up horses, at least one will be forced to race out of their comfort zone, and the runner who ends up on the wrong end of that scramble could be compromised for the remainder of the race.

Northern Brave's 43-day absence for Michael Dods is notable — if he returns short of peak fitness over this extended 1m4f trip, he could fade badly from the two-furlong pole having been competitive to that point.

Ludo's Landing carries 142lbs, the highest weight in the field — if the race turns into a proper sprint finish, monitor whether that burden blunts his change of gear in the final furlong against three lightly-weighted 3yos.

The entire field has Good going marked as OK — no horse holds a going advantage, meaning the race is unlikely to be decided by ground suitability and finishing class or positional luck will be the differentiating factor.

races.name: John Joseph Robson Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has modest recent form (best of 3rd last five) and is naturally a hold-up horse thrust onto the lead by default — his pace figures to be sustainable rather than scorching, but that is exactly what makes him dangerous as the nominal pace-setter; penalty weight of 134lbs and 23 days since last run are manageable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bay Breeze — ranked bottom of nine on our figures — has managed just a third three starts back amid a sequence of mid-pack efforts; experience over today's trip and going offers some comfort, but he faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Fanjove
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old has placed at 6f on standard going in its best effort and carries the style burden of being a genuine hold-up horse forced further forward than ideal in this compressed field; the jockey claim (3lb) from Jack Callan helps with the weights, but only two runs from 13 on comparable going (0W0P) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out and nothing better than a second in recent starts, Fanjove makes little appeal ranked eighth of nine on our figures; he has run over today's trip before, and stall one is his sole neutral angle.

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's seven-year-old has a win and three places from ten runs on similar going and knows how to finish, but being shifted away from its natural rearward position into midfield complicates matters; recent form reads 5-9-7-7-8 and the horse has not threatened at the sharp end lately.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and beaten well in three of those, Lord Abama at least has experience of today's trip and conditions; 46 days off and 130 lb to carry make the task no easier, though a rating of 67 suggests he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's four-year-old showed a solid 3rd at 6f on good ground in recent history and wears tongue-tie plus cheekpieces, but the trainer's current strike rate (0/26 over 14 days) is a cold stat; the horse is a true hold-up type being mapped forward and at 137lbs is not lightly weighted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and coming off a ninth last time out, Maldevious has run over today's trip and going before, but a struggling trainer on 0/26 in the past fortnight is a notable negative against a filly drawn in stall nine carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Khabib
runners_data.note: Ray Craggs's eight-year-old has four placed efforts from ten similar-going starts and clearly handles the conditions, but recent form includes an 8th and a 9th and its natural desire to race from the rear is compromised in this field; the 5lb claim from Cian Horgan is worth noting as a potential small compensator.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and beaten a long way last time out, Khabib nonetheless boasts prior experience over today's trip and going, and a speed rating of 78 hints at latent ability — the worry is those back-to-back poor runs returning here after 46 days off.

runners_data.name: Mecca's Symphony
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's four-year-old has three placed efforts on good ground and is stepping down to 6f from a 7f comfort zone — that trip shortening suits a horse with hold-up tendencies and a strong late finish; the tongue-tie is applied and recent form (3-7-2-0-7 at 7f) suggests inconsistency, but a furlong less could sharpen the finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Mecca's Symphony faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second two starts back offers a sliver of encouragement after 43 days off.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a key booking for Ross Burdon's six-year-old, and with two wins and three places from eight good-ground runs the horse's course profile is solid; visor applied and a 1/7f win on good ground in the last five runs shows it can quicken, with 21 days between runs suggesting freshness.
runners_data.comment: Northcliff won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving him solid claims from stall two off a workable official mark of 65; the concern is an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's four-year-old is lightly raced on good ground yet has two wins and three places from 11 comparable starts, and a recent 6f win (form figure: 1) signals live, sharp fitness only 12 days ago; at 139lbs it carries top weight but Jonathan England's booking keeps costs down and the horse's profile suits the anticipated moderate-tempo sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and back in good time on 12 days' rest, Great has experience over today's trip and going and rates above his official mark. The fifth last time out keeps expectations in check, but conditions suit and he makes solid appeal from stall three at 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old is one of the sharpest horses in the field on form — a win at 7f and a 2nd at 6f in the last five on good ground — and 10 days since its last run means it arrives race-fit; Cam Hardie is a capable booking and the horse's recent placed and winning form over 6-7f on good going is exactly what this race shape is likely to reward.
runners_data.comment: Kings Merchant arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a close second three starts back, looking fit on a quick ten-day turnaround and with experience of both today's trip and going; the risk is that fourth last time out suggests he may not have built on that sequence.

races.paceDynamic: Bay Breeze is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front despite being a natural hold-up horse, meaning this 6f at Thirsk is likely to be run at a sustainable, uncontested tempo rather than a searching gallop. With no genuine front-runner to push Bay Breeze along, the early fractions figure to be modest, setting up a race that develops late and rewards horses with a powerful finishing kick rather than those who want a true test of stamina or a frenetic pace. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Fanjove, Maldevious, Khabib, Mecca's Symphony and Lord Abama all want to race from the rear but are mapped further forward than their natural role, meaning the pace dynamic is compressed and the race shape will be tight and tactical. The dominant beneficiary profile here is the horse with the best late acceleration who can pick off a moderate-tempo field in the final furlong — genuine closers with good-ground form and a strong jockey booking are best placed, with Northcliff, Great and Kings Merchant the most naturally suited given their form and style fit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the field bunches turning for home, a powerful late finisher benefits from the moderate gallop.
scenarios.body: Bay Breeze's unforced lead means the field travels well within itself until the two-furlong pole, when those with genuine acceleration can sprint clear; horses with confirmed good-ground form over 6f and strong finishing kicks are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Fail to Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses fail to secure clear daylight and get boxed in as the field compresses, only the horse who travels widest or most freely can deliver a challenge.
scenarios.body: The tactical nightmare of too many hold-up types in a small 9-runner field means traffic is a genuine risk late, and the horse who takes a positive, prompt position from the gate avoids the problem; Kings Merchant and Great, who have both won recently and carry fitness, are best equipped.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Midway
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze is pressured or the pace quickens significantly from the halfway point, the race becomes a true test of stamina-speed for 6f.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace injection would sort the field on merit and disadvantage the hold-up horses racing out of role, benefiting those who can travel close to the pace and sustain their effort; Northcliff's win record at 7f on good ground and Maldevious's strong 6f form both become relevant.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Collects Blindside
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is exceptionally slow and chaos erupts in the final furlong, a lower-weighted horse with underrated form collects in the bunched finish.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian tempo can compress the entire field and allow a runner at the lower end of the weights to benefit from the sprint finish regardless of natural style; Fanjove's previous placed form at 6f at a standard trip and Mecca's Symphony's three placed efforts in similar company offer some residual claims.

watchPoints.text: Northcliff and Great carry top weights of 139lbs each — watch whether Silvestre De Sousa or Jonathan England take a positive early position to avoid the traffic compression inevitable when so many hold-up horses are squeezed into midfield.

Bay Breeze's redistribution to the lead is artificial — if the horse reverts to its natural hold-up tendency and drifts back from the gate, there is no confirmed early pace in this race and the tempo could become dangerously slow, flattening out finishing differences.

Khabib and Lord Abama are both mapped forward of their true preferred position — watch for both to drift back early and create a crowding scenario in the rear third of the field, which could affect Fanjove and Mecca's Symphony who want similar ground.

Kings Merchant arrives on a very quick turnaround (10 days) after a competitive outing — watch for any signs of staleness or whether Cam Hardie is instructed to be bold from the stalls to exploit the lack of genuine early pace.

Mecca's Symphony drops from 7f to 6f for the first time in recent runs — watch whether the shorter trip sharpens its finish or catches it out positionally, as a hold-up horse at 6f on a flat track needs the pace to be fair to collect late.
